header: The management page: one page that lists, as titles that open them, every management tool the signed-in person may use (the Employee manager, the PAX directory editor, the Holiday, Circular and Announcement managers, the Contact access log). It opens when "management", "management page", "admin", "managers"... is typed. not signed in -> "Please log in", and nothing about the tools signed in, no authority -> "Not allowed", and nothing about the tools the HOD of C&IT -> all of them a delegate -> only the tools the HOD gave him (a withdrawn one is gone at once: asked from the database on every request) I made the two refusals not plain sentences but a small card of their own (src/components/ManagementHubPanel.tsx, ManagementGatePanel): "login" has a Sign in button that opens the login window (and when the person has signed in the same question is asked again by itself, so the page, or the refusal, comes up without typing anything); "denied" says, in the same words whether the person was signed in already or has just signed in, that he is not authorised. The list is only a convenience. The tool itself checks its authority again when a title is opened (a title types the tool's own phrase into the search bar, and the tool's own responder asks the database who is asking), so the page can never open more than the person may use. Who is asking is always the login: the route ignores a ticket sent by the browser. This file is PURE apart from the `authorities` and `nameOf` that the caller gives (src/lib/facility/hubAccess.ts gives the database's).

symbols.name: detectManagementHubIntent
doc: "management", "management page", "admin", "admin tools", "open the management pages", "all managers", "administration": I take a line made ONLY of the words above, with at least one of management, manager or admin, as the page. A line with any other word ("employee management", "how to become a manager", "circular admin") is not the page: it belongs to that tool, or it is an ordinary question.

behaviours: every management tool of the kit has a line on the page (what it is for, the words that open it), and the page has no line for a tool that does not exist
the words that open the tools are all different
a title opens its OWN tool: the words of each tool are read by that tool's own reader, and by no other tool's
a tool's words are not taken for the management page, and the page's words are not taken by any tool
the line that asks for the page: management, admin and the like, with only filler words
any other line is not the page: a tool's own words, a question that has the word manager in it, a person's title, a lone 'tools'
the search line's own readers do not take these words first (no calculator hint, no other tool): the page is reached by Enter like any search
not signed in: the sign-in card (state login), no tool is named, and the database is not even asked
a blank ticket is not signed in either: the sign-in card, and the database is not asked
signed in but holding no tool: the refusal card (state denied), no tool is named
the HOD of C&IT: all six tools, in the usual order, held as hod, with his name
a delegate sees ONLY what the HOD gave him: circular and holiday, not the other four; and he is shown as a delegate
a withdrawn delegation is gone at once: the same person, asked again after the HOD withdrew circular, sees holiday only
when the database cannot be asked, nobody gets in (closed, not open)
a line that is not the page is not answered by it, and the database is not asked
the name is optional (a person with no name found still gets the page)
toolsOf keeps the usual order whatever order the rights were given in
the HOD is known by ticket: all six as hod, and the delegate table is not asked
a delegate holds the tools of his rows; a row for a tool that does not exist is ignored
the question leaves out withdrawn delegations (revoked_at IS NULL) and asks by the ticket given, not by anything else
a blank ticket holds nothing and asks nothing
the panel lists the titles as buttons, one for each tool held (and no other), each with what it is for; a delegate is told he sees only what he was given
for the HOD it shows six titles and says he holds all of them
the page is asked for before every tool's own request, so no tool's phrase can reach it first, and it is drawn first in the answer area
pressing a title searches for the tool's own words (the tool then checks the person again)
who is asking is the login's ticket: the responder is given the route's ticket and the page never reads one from the line

typing any of the page's words shows 'Press Enter to open the management page' under the box, like the other keywords: the hint uses the SAME reader as the server (so every word that opens the page also shows it), and it goes once the line has been sent
a management tool's page has a Back button, the SAME button as the calculators' pages (same arrow, same word, same classes: one component, BackButton), saying where it goes: the management page
BackButton says its destination to the screen reader and in the tooltip

the Back button is shown above every one of the six tools' pages and not on the management page, and it goes back by searching for 'management' (which the server answers with the page, after checking the login again)
the management page has the cross of the calculators' pages: the SAME button (same classes, one component, CloseButton), at the right of the header, saying what it closes

the cross does what the calculators' cross does: it closes the page and leaves what was typed in the box (when the page came from the Admin button the cross also wipes the box and returns the choice to Everything: closeManagement) (clearSearch drops the answer and the sent line, not the text), so 'Press Enter to open the management page' is there again
the six tools' pages keep their Back button and have no cross of their own added (the management page's cross is on the page itself)
the guide's What-to-type list has an entry for the management page, and every word it gives is one the page really answers to (the guide cannot promise a word that does nothing)

all the cards are the same size: the grid's rows share the height of the tallest card (auto-rows-fr), each cell holds its card at full height (li flex, button h-full w-full), and the card's own sizes are in rem and relative units only (no fixed pixel width or height)

THE MANAGEMENT PAGE HAS THE CALCULATORS' FRAME: the same soft gradient and rounded corners, and the same two blurred lights (the bluish glow behind the top-right cross: a sky light at the top right), not a plain white card

the header is the calculators' too: the gradient icon tile with its white ring, the title, the line under it, the role chip, then the cross; and no privacy/approximation notice (the page has nothing to type into)
SIGNED OUT: the HOD, a delegate and anybody else are all asked to sign in, by the same card, the database is not asked, and nobody is told who may or may not have the page
SIGNED OUT card: the same payload for every signed-out line (login, no name, no tool, no role)
AFTER SIGNING IN the same line gives the page to the HOD and to a delegate, and the refusal to anybody else
SIGNED IN and not authorised: the refusal; and it is the same refusal whether the person was signed in all along or has just signed in (the same payload for the same person)
the refusal names the person to himself ('signed in as ...') and nobody else; a refusal with no name found is still the refusal
the sign-in card: a lock, the title, the sentence, a Sign in BUTTON, and the line that an unauthorised person will be told so after signing in; it is in the calculators' frame, with the cross
the refusal card: 'You are not authorised to access this page' and the sentence, announced to a screen reader (role alert), NO Sign in button, the person's name; same frame and cross
the sign-in card has no button when it cannot open the window (no handler given): it never shows a button that does nothing
neither card names a management tool, a role or who holds what
the Sign in button opens the app's login window (the same openModal the other sign-in prompts use), and the card is drawn before the page, so a refusal never shows the page
signing in asks the question again by itself: the search's key includes the login's ticket, so a new login fetches the answer anew

PRESSING ENTER on the page's words sends the search at once: that branch comes BEFORE the 'which utility do you mean' question to the AI (a call to the model with 'Understanding your request' on the screen) and the people name search, and uses neither
FETCH AHEAD uses the SAME address as the real search (one function, searchKey, builds both), so the answer fetched ahead is found at once when the title is pressed
fetching ahead changes nothing on screen and asks only when the modal is open and the text is a real search (3 letters or more); a failure is swallowed (the press then searches as before)

each title fetches its page ahead when the pointer comes, when it is touched or pressed down, and when it gets the keyboard focus; the page's tools still check the person themselves when answering (nothing is opened from the browser's side)
